Sonny Gray (18-5, 2.72 ERA) finished his marvelous regular season with another strong performance, firing six shutout innings on 77 pitches, allowing four hits and one walk while striking out three. Next start? Game 1 or 2 of next week’s AL Wild Card Series, all but certain to be at Yankee Stadium.
“He looked fantastic,” said Red Sox manager Chad Tracy. “Had his spin. Was in the zone. Was ahead in the count. He looked really good. It was good to see.”
Even better to see was the return of All-Star closer Aroldis Chapman, who hadn’t pitched since Sept. 13 because of a lat issue. All the 38-year-old did was overpower the Guardians by striking out the side (all swinging) in order on 12 pitches. That’s all it took for career save No. 402 and 35th this season.
“I felt good and happy to be able to go out there,” said Chapman. “I felt like my pitches and my stuff were very good today. So I’m happy to be back. I feel normal. I feel like I’m at 100 percent right now.”
That is certainly good news for the Red Sox, who need their closer in top form to make a deep postseason run.
“He looked sharp,” said Tracy. “That was also really good to see.”
For the first time in weeks, Tracy was able to deploy his 7-8-9 relief crew in Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock and Chapman. All three relievers had injuries at various times down the stretch but are trending well now.
“That was great,” said Tracy. “To be perfectly honest with you, that was kind of planned out regardless of how the game went. So to be able to score a run prior to that section of relievers coming in was fantastic.”
And while hits with runners in scoring position (2-for-14, 11 left on base) were again a rare commodity for Boston, Andruw Monasterio broke out of an 0-for-21 slump by belting an RBI single with two outs in the sixth that scored Jarren Duran from second.
In a game in which neither team had an extra-base hit, combining instead for 17 singles, Monasterio’s knock was the difference in the ballgame.
“I was fighting myself just yesterday and tonight about my approach,” said Monasterio. “I just had to get through it. And I did it.”
In this final homestand of the regular season, the main focus for the Red Sox is having their house in order for what’s to come next week.
There was some cause for concern in that regard, as center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela, after his first at-bat back from a three-week absence with a right quadriceps strain, had to exit in the top of the third with right hamstring tightness.
The Red Sox are hopeful it was a mild setback.
“I think it was just a cramp,” said Rafaela. “Maybe not hydrated enough. And I got that cramp right there and just didn't want to risk going for the double. And then, obviously, it’s Trace just trying to protect me, with big things in front of us. And so I think it's just that.”

The Boston Red Sox pulled off a 1-0 series-evening win over the visiting Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday night, despite the ongoing dearth of situational hitting that has plagued them for the last two weeks and intermittently throughout the season.
Boston batters tallied 12 hits, but went 2 for 14 with runners in scoring position, and left 11 men on base in eight innings.
Fortunately for the home team, Sonny Gray was on form in his final start of the regular season. The veteran right-hander tossed six shutout innings, with four hits, one walk and three strikeouts.
Gray’s sixth scoreless start of at least six innings this year tied his single-season high first set in 2015 and matched in 2025. He is the first Red Sox pitcher to make at least six such starts in his age-36 season or older since Luis Tiant in 1977, and only the fourth in franchise history (also Cy Young, Lefty Grove).
“Just a really good pitcher,” manager Chad Tracy said of his starter. “The level of consistency for him from start to finish has been very fun to watch, and impressive.”
Though Gray’s pitch count sat at 77 (52 for strikes) after the sixth and the game remained scoreless, Tracy went to his bullpen. With Boston’s postseason ticket punched on Sunday, the short hook could suggest Gray is getting the ball for Game 1 of the Wild Card series on Tuesday.
Cleveland southpaw Foster Griffin was not nearly as adept at keeping the Red Sox off the diamond. He struck out seven and issued no walks, but yielded 10 hits in six innings of one-run ball.
Save for Jarren Duran’s leadoff single and Andruw Monasterio’s two-out RBI single in the sixth, the Red Sox bailed Griffin out every time. They were 2 for 11 RISP through his six innings. Their nine men left on base during Griffin’s start included multiple in four of the first five frames and bases-loaded in the third.
“Yeah, I mean, take the positives,” Tracy said of the offense. “I thought we swung the bat great. We actually got some hits today. … Between (the two-out hits) and the accumulation of hits and base runners throughout the game, I thought it was a pretty good offensive night. Obviously you’d like to score more, but we did take better plate appearances.”
Tyron Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman, Boston’s elite bullpen trio all season long, ensured the slim lead held until the end with a scoreless inning apiece. Tracy revealed postgame their appearances were “planned out, regardless of how the game went.”
“That was great,” Tracy said. “To be able to score a run prior to that section of relievers coming in was fantastic.”
Duran, who replaced Ceddanne Rafaela in center field in the top of the third, led off the bottom of the eighth with a single. His subsequent steal of second made 2026 his second career season with 20 home runs and 20 stolen bases (also 2024). Duran, Mookie Betts and Jackie Jensen are the only players in franchise history with multiple 20-20 seasons.
Rafaela’s first game back from a 10-day stint on the injured list with a right quad strain began in energetic fashion. He recorded each of the first three outs, including a diving catch to rob Guardians hitter Steven Kwan of a leadoff single.
But after pulling up lame at first base on his own leadoff single in the bottom of the second, Rafaela ultimately left the game with right hamstring tightness when the inning turned over. Tracy announced postgame that Rafaela will undergo an MRI on Thursday.
“No, I think it’s more frustrating (than disappointing),” Tracy said of the Rafaela situation. “You want to see everybody get to that finish line healthy.
“So more just when you see it, you’re concerned, you know? So (we) don’t know where we’re at with it yet. Hopefully, it’s not a huge deal, but still, yeah, makes your heart jump a little bit, and we’ll see where he’s at.”
Cleveland threatened against Whitlock in an eighth inning that saw both teams run out of ABS challenges. No. 9 hitter Brayan Rocchio led off with a single, and Whitlock issued a one-out walk to third baseman José Ramírez before getting an inning-ending double play from designated hitter Chase DeLauter.
After the Red Sox stranded Duran in the bottom of the eighth, Chapman took the mound for the first time since Sept. 13. Boston’s All-Star closer was back in top form after being day-to-day with lat tightness. He struck out the side, Jo Adell, and pinch-hitters Angel Martínez and Angel Genao on 12 pitches.
The Red Sox are 85-73 with four games left to play. Wednesday marked Tracy’s first win since the interim tag was removed on Tuesday.

In the sixth, Jarren Duran (2-for-3) lined a leadoff single to left and moved to second on a groundout. He scored from second base on Monasterio’s knock, sliding ahead of left fielder Steven Kwan’s relay throw and catcher Patrick Bailey’s tag.
Gray (18-5) struck out three while allowing four hits and one walk to increase his American League-leading win total. Tyron Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman each threw a scoreless inning to finish off Boston’s 17th shutout victory of the season.
Chapman struck out the side in the ninth to log his 35th save as Boston snapped a three-game losing streak.
Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela returned from a 17-game injury absence caused by a right quad strain to record all three outs in the first, including a spectacular diving catch on Kwan, the leadoff hitter who still went 2-for-4 for Cleveland (82-76).
Griffin worked six frames, striking out seven and allowing one run on 10 hits and no walks.
The Guardians remained one game up on the White Sox (81-77) in the American League Central after Chicago lost 5-4 at Kansas City on Wednesday.
Rafaela hit a leadoff single in the second inning but appeared to be in pain after reaching first. He stayed in the game to run the bases and initially took his defensive position before Duran replaced him. The Red Sox announced that Rafaela was dealing with right hamstring tightness.
Rafaela’s defense helped Gray retire the first six men he faced. Bailey recorded Cleveland’s first hit with a leadoff single in the third, but a 6-3 double play ended the inning without any damage. Gray fanned a pair of Guardians to strand two to end the fourth.
After the lone run scored and Gray exited, Guerrero struck out three in the seventh after a leadoff walk. Whitlock worked around Brayan Rocchio’s leadoff single and Jose Ramirez’s one-out walk in the eighth, inducing an inning-ending double-play grounder from Chase DeLauter.

The end of the MLB Season is almost here, with roughly five games remaining, including today, for most teams. There are still some exciting matchups today and this weekend. We went just 1-1 yesterday, with a loss on the Angels and a win in the Rays-Yankees game. I suppose I should know better than to back a 100-loss team.
Tonight, I’m going for a game that we could potentially see in the playoffs as the Guardians take on the Red Sox.
The Guardians are currently the owners of the top spot in the American League Central. As seems to be the case for Cleveland every season, they saved their best baseball for the end of the season. They’ve won six straight games, but they are only one game ahead of the White Sox, who have also won three straight games. The good news for both of them is that, as long as they both are winning games, they can both make the postseason. The magic number for the Guardians to make the playoffs is down to one.
Giving them a great chance today is the arm they acquired at the trade deadline, Foster Griffin. For the season, Griffin is 15-5 with a 3.67 ERA and a 1.19 WHIP. Griffin, overall, has been a nice addition to the team. He has two starts that were a little bit of a disaster, going four innings against the Mets and allowing five earned in his debut with the Guardians.
The Baltimore Orioles also knocked him around for eight runs in 2.1 innings. His other six starts saw him going for 22 innings and allow just 11 runs. He has never faced the Red Sox, so he could have them off balance the first time through the lineup.
The Boston Red Sox are one of those teams that are likely brimming with confidence. After a disaster of a start to their season, they pivoted and became one of the hottest teams in baseball right before the All-Star Break. They continue to be a streaky team, but the majority of their streaks have seen them winning games instead of losing them. They are still just an average team at Fenway with a 38-38 record for the season. It is almost hard to believe given how good they’ve been, but getting to .500 is impressive because of how bad they were early in the year.
The Red Sox are sending the one guy who was dominant at home all year, Sonny Gray. For the season, Sonny Gray is 17-5 with a 2.82 ERA and a 1.16 WHIP. He should be in the running for the Cy Young Award, even though he won’t win over Cam Schlittler. He’s been solid in September, going 19.1 innings and allowing a total of six earned runs. He faced the Guardians earlier this season and allowed just one earned run over six innings in a 9-1 win for the Red Sox.
It wasn’t just that one game against the Guardians that Gray has excelled in. He has been great against them for years, holding hitters to a .208 batting average over 130 at-bats. Although the Red Sox don’t really “need” this game to solidify their Wild Card spot, they still should look to win. Gray has been dominant for them, and they’ve been very successful in his outings this year. I’m backing the Red Sox here and I also think they probably cover the -1.5 run line. I also would be surprised to see this game go under 6.5 runs. I’ll play all three bets.

The Boston Red Sox kept outfielder Jarren Duran out of the starting lineup again Wednesday night as they hosted the Cleveland Guardians in the second game of a three-game series at Fenway Park.
Manager Chad Tracy’s posted batting order featured Roman Anthony in left field, Nick Sogard at first base, Jahmai Jones as the designated hitter, Wilyer Abreu in right field, Adley Rutschman behind the plate, Ceddanne Rafaela in center field, Caleb Durbin at third base, Trevor Story at shortstop and Andruw Monasterio at second base. Sonny Gray was listed as the starting pitcher.
Duran also sat Tuesday, when the Guardians beat the Red Sox 3-2. He entered that game as a pinch-hitter and drew a walk.
Cleveland took the series opener on Nathaniel Lowe’s sacrifice fly in the ninth inning. The Guardians stranded 15 runners but still extended their winning streak to six games.
Boston dropped to 84-73. The club already clinched an American League Wild Card berth Sunday but has lost three straight and eight of its last 12.
Duran entered Wednesday batting .204 with 110 hits, 20 home runs, 69 RBIs, 65 runs and 19 stolen bases in 146 games. He had 538 at-bats, 39 walks and 163 strikeouts.
The left-handed hitter has struggled in September. He was 9-for-50 with one home run and one RBI in 17 games this month before Tuesday’s appearance.
Over his last 15 games he was 8-for-42 with one homer. His on-base-plus-slugging percentage sat at .625 for the season.
Rafaela’s return to center field tightened the outfield picture. Anthony has been starting in left and Abreu in right, leaving Duran as the extra outfielder in many recent games.
Tracy had the interim tag removed Tuesday and was named the franchise’s 49th manager. The Red Sox have used a mix of platoons and rest days for Duran down the stretch.
Gray brings a 17-5 record and 2.82 ERA into the start. Cleveland is expected to counter with Forrest Griffin.
The Guardians sit at 82-75 and hold a one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox in the AL Central. Chicago owns the season-series tiebreaker.
Duran, 30, is in his sixth major league season, all with Boston. He was an All-Star in 2024.
He still ranks among the team leaders in home runs and RBIs despite the low batting average. His 20 homers leave him one short of his career high.
The Red Sox close the regular season with this series, then host the Chicago Cubs for three games. Seeding and rest for the Wild Card round remain in play.
Duran’s speed and defense have kept him in the mix even as his batting average dropped. He stole 19 bases and continued to play a plus outfield when used.
Boston’s offense produced eight hits Tuesday. Rutschman went 3-for-4 and pinch-hitter Mickey Gasper tied the game with a home run in the eighth.
Cleveland collected 12 hits. Angel Martínez finished 3-for-4.
The Red Sox sit 12 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East. The Yankees hold the other Wild Card spot six games ahead of Boston.
Duran’s role for the final week and any postseason series will depend on how Tracy balances the four outfielders available.

The Craig Breslow era in Boston has felt like a roller coaster ride. Hired at the start of the 2023-24 offseason, the Boston Red Sox have not had a losing season under Breslow, despite wild swings in the team's form over the three years.
With the Red Sox clinching a playoff berth for the second year in a row, team ownership decided that now was the time to exercise two options on their Chief Baseball Officer's contract, guaranteeing his deal for the 2029 and 2030 seasons. On the surface, a head of baseball operations who got his team to the playoffs in years two and three of their time running the club getting years added to their contract, would make sense, but in Breslow's case it isn't as straightforward.
It was only three months ago when most of Red Sox Nation was calling for Breslow's head. The Red Sox were 32-46 on June 24, dead last in the division, and it already seemed like the season was over. It took a miraculous turnaround to get the team to the playoffs. Not to say that Breslow had nothing to do with that; he had added a lot of players to the roster who were key contributors, but that has a lot more to do with the players and coaches than the front office.
Breslow's tenure has also been marred by controversy, specifically the Rafael Devers drama. It was his handling of the situation, along with former manager Alex Cora, that ultimately led to the fracture of the relationship with the team's then-face of the franchise. While the fanbase was split on whose side they took, player or team, his actions after the fact didn't make it any better.
Red Sox's Craig Breslow had the hottest seat of any GM only three months ago
It was the signing of Alex Bregman that caused the Devers drama in the first place. While Breslow was praised for the signing, Bregman opted out at the end of the year and was then not re-signed. The Red Sox went from two elite third basemen to none in the span of a season. It wasn't a good look for the Red Sox CBO.
Now, Breslow's pivot from all of the drama and mess surrounding Devers and Bregman looks incredibly good in hindsight. The additions of Ranger Suarez, Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Caleb Durbin, and others have been extremely impactful to the Red Sox's success this season. While some of those moves were celebrated at the time they happened, others like the Durbin-Kyle Harrison swap (that also netted the Red Sox Andruw Monasterio and Anthony Seigler) were heavily scrutinized.
Breslow also made good moves at the trade deadline, adding Erik Miller and Eli White, who have looked good for the Sox. He also made the splash trade for Adley Rutschman, which hasn't worked as well on the field, but certainly instilled confidence in the team, knowing the front office believed in them.
Red Sox could've softened the impact by extending one of Craig Breslow's options at first
All of this is to say that Breslow's time as CBO hasn't been as smooth sailing as the records would suggest. He has had some high highs but also some low lows. Why did ownership feel the need to exercise both options right now? The first option wasn't needed until the 2029 season, two years out. The second was for 2030, three years out.
Doing the first one now would've been fine — picking up the 2029 option gives Breslow another three comfortable seasons on his contract. That would make him more comfortable making moves for the future and give him the job security to know he will likely be in place to see them play out. Selecting the 2030 option on the same day was unnecessary, though.
There have been too many hiccups in the three years under Breslow to say he has warranted another four seasons. The start of 2026 could easily repeat itself in 2027. Should ownership feel the need to relieve him of his duties early, then this makes it that much harder. Breslow hasn't won a World Series in Boston; in fact, he hasn't even made it out of the Wild Card round. Exercising the option for 2030 feels very premature.
Breslow has not done a bad job in Boston. At the end of the day, it's results that matter, and Breslow's teams have made the playoffs two out of three times. He shouldn't be fearing for his job, but his contract also wasn't ending for another two seasons. It feels early to be handing him the keys so far down the road after the drama of his first two years as CBO.

Baseball season’s marathon is coming down to its final sprint this week, and the Guardians are going to find out if they have enough figurative speed to finish on the podium.
The Guardians did the hard work over the weekend by sweeping the Oakland/Sacramento/not-yet Las Vegas Athletics — though they had to come back on Sept. 18 and 19 — and squeaking out a 1-0 win. But style points don’t matter. Plus-one in the win column is all that counts.
The Detroit Tigers begrudgingly gave Cleveland the slightest bit of help by overcoming a six-run first inning to beat the Chicago White Sox on Sept. 18, 11-8. Unfortunately, their offense didn’t make much noise after that comeback, but it gave the Guardians just enough to climb back atop the AL Central alone.
Now, Cleveland takes its one-game lead in the AL Central and a five-game winning streak to Boston to face the freshly playoff-clinched Red Sox for three games. A series at Boston vs. the Red Sox is almost inarguably the toughest series left for Cleveland, the White Sox, and the rest of the wild card orbit of Texas, Toronto and Houston.
The White Sox will head to Kansas City this week, where the Royals are above .500 at home. Then they come back home to host the Colorado Rockies to end the regular season.
Unfortunately for the Guardians, they don’t have the safety net of any tiebreakers against teams in their orbit. A sweep of the Red Sox would give them the tiebreaker over Boston, but that wouldn’t matter as it would keep them in first place in the division going into the final weekend anyway.
The Red Sox also have their rotation lined up for the wild card Series, likely with the Yankees, since they’re close to having that locked in. Meaning Cleveland gets to face Boston’s best starting arms in Peyton Tolle, ace Sonny Gray, and another lefty in Ranger Suarez. So they all have six days of rest lined up into their starts in three-game wild card series.
Boston is six games back in the loss column of the New York Yankees, so catching them is highly improbable. Will that mean the Red Sox will get some players to rest? Possibly. They might be unlikely to push their starters too hard. But then that’s up to the Guardians’ offense to put them in that position to decide.
By virtue of holding Williams back to pitch last week in the opener vs. the White Sox, he’s not scheduled to pitch again until at least September 25 or 26. Cleveland has Parker Messick going vs. Boston in the opener, which also lines him up for regular rest on the final day of the season on Sept. 27, should Cleveland still need to win that game to get in the postseason.
The division title would be the most advantageous path for Cleveland. It would get a bye to the ALDS and host it at home, though the Guardians just did get their at-home record one game above .500 thanks to a 5-1 home stand to wrap up the regular season at Progressive Field. There is also a scenario in which Texas catches fire this week and clinches the second seed as the AL West champ and relegates Cleveland to a wild-card series no matter what. But for the Guardians, everything right now is about being one game better.
If they manage to win the division, then they can line the rotation up how they want for the ALDS.
If they are still fighting for a wild-card spot heading into the weekend in Kansas City, they would need to decide how they need to use Williams and Messick. If WIlliams starts on September 25, he could go in Game 2 of the wild card series on Sept. 30. If Messick has to pitch for the wild-card spot on Sept. 27, that takes him out of the wild-card round rotation at least on regular rest. At the very least, Cleveland needs the wild card spot wrapped up by Sept. 26, so it can skip Messick on Sept. 27, push him to Sept. 29 and have Messick and Williams lined up for Games 1 and 2.
The Guardians will either finish with another AL Central title, the franchise’s third in a row and the 14th in the history of the division, dating to its first in 1995, the last wild card spot, sending them to the worst division winner, possibly Houston or Texas, and then onto the White Sox IF they get past the wild card round. That means this final road trip could be a four-city, two-week tour to play the most meaningful and stressful baseball all year.
Or: They could miss the playoffs entirely. Thinking about some of those losses earlier in the year at St. Louis and Juan Brito’s error and one of the few Cade Smith blown saves. Or another one of his blown saves during the sweep by the Mets with two outs at home after the trade deadline.
Without having any tiebreakers over teams competing for playoff spots with them, the Guardians have to be one game better than any of them for a playoff spot. Be it the division or the wild card. That means winning one game at a time and just needing to be one run and one game better.

Cristopher Sánchez consigue su 18ma victoria, líder de MLB; Juan Soto se va de 4-1
El dominicano Cristopher Sánchez consiguió su 18.ª victoria, la mayor cantidad en las Grandes Ligas, para guiar la victoria el domingo 7-2 de los Filis de Filadelfia ante los Mets de Nueva York.
Los Filis (86-70), que rescataron un empate en la serie de cuatro juegos, llegaron al domingo en el tercer puesto de comodín de la Liga Nacional, a un juego de los Cachorros de Chicago y Padres de San Diego y con una ventaja de cuatro juegos sobre los Diamondbacks de Arizona.
Sánchez permitió seis hits —incluido el jonrón de Bo Bichette en la sexta entrada— y ponchó a seis en 6 1/3 innings, con lo que rompió el empate con Sonny Gray, de los Medias Rojas de Boston, por el liderato de victorias en las Grandes Ligas.
El último lanzador de los Filis en liderar las mayores en victorias fue Steve Carlton, con 23 en 1982.
Justin Crawford conectó un triple de tres carreras y el venezolano Luis Arráez terminó con dos carreras impulsadas. Alec Bohm y Trea Turner aportaron cada uno un hit productor. Kyle Schwarber igualó su máximo de carrera con cuatro bases por bolas.
El novato Jonah Tong (2-2) permitió cuatro carreras y ponchó a cinco en 4 2/3 innings por los coleros Mets, que terminaron 36-45 en casa —su peor registro en Citi Field desde 2013, que fue de 33-48.
Los Mets atrajeron a 2.712.120 aficionados esta temporada, una caída de 5.870 aficionados por juego respecto a la temporada pasada —el descenso más pronunciado en las Grandes Ligas.
El dominicano Juan Soto bateó de 4-1.

NEW YORK (AP) — Cristopher Sánchez earned his major league-leading 18th win Sunday, leading the Philadelphia Phillies to a 7-2 victory over the New York Mets.
The Phillies (86-70), who salvaged a split of the four-game series, entered Sunday in the third National League wild-card spot, one game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres and four games clear of the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Sánchez surrendered six hits — including Bo Bichette’s sixth-inning homer — and struck out six over 6 1/3 innings as he snapped a tie with the Boston Red Sox’s Sonny Gray for the big league lead in wins.

The last Phillies pitcher to lead the majors in wins was Steve Carlton with 23 in 1982.
Justin Crawford had a three-run triple and Luis Arraez finished with two RBIs. Alec Bohm and Trea Turner each had run-scoring hits. Kyle Schwarber tied a career high with four walks.
Rookie Jonah Tong (2-2) gave up four runs and struck out five in 4 2/3 innings for the last-place Mets, who finished 36-45 at home — their worst record at Citi Field since the 2013 team went 33-48.
PIRATES 4, ROYALS 3
PITTSBURGH (AP) — Rafael Flores Jr. hit the go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to help Pittsburgh to a win over Kansas City and complete a series sweep.
After Ryan O’Hearn led off with a single to center, Flores sent a slider from Nate Pearson (2-3) into the left-field bleachers for his 10th homer this season.
Pittsburgh rallied with a two-run homer in the eighth for a second straight day. Brandon Lowe had his 33rd of the season in a 6-5 win Saturday.
Carmen Mlodzinki (8-7) got the win. He allowed two runs and three hits in three innings. The reliever gave up a pinch-hit, two-run home run to Vinnie Pasquantino that gave Kansas City a 3-2 lead with two outs in the seventh.
Mason Montgomery earned his 16th save. He retired the first two batters in the ninth before Luke Maile hit a double and took third on a fielding error by Jake Mangum. Montgomery got Isaac Collins to fly out to right to strand Maile.
The Royals went ahead 1-0 in the first inning with three straight singles off Lake Bachar. Bobby Witt Jr. beat out a groundball to second baseman Lowe. He moved to third on a single to right from Jac Caglianone and scored when Perez shot one through the middle of the infield.
RAYS 5, RED SOX 1
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Griffin Jax tossed five shutout innings and the Tampa Bay crept closer to the AL East title with a victory over Boston.
The Rays will have an opportunity to clinch the franchise’s fifth division title during Tuesday’s doubleheader at the New York Yankees.
Boston would have clinched a playoff spot with a victory. The Red Sox, who were 32-46 and 15 1/2 games back in the AL East on June 24, have since gone 52-25. They could still wrap up a spot Sunday with a Houston loss.
Jax (8-10) allowed three singles and worked out of a bases-loaded jam in the fifth inning by striking out Roman Anthony. Cole Sulser, Brody Hopkins and Steven Matz each pitched an inning of scoreless relief.
Boston’s Trevor Story spoiled the shutout in the ninth with a one-out home run off right-hander Ty Johnson.
The Rays scored four first-inning runs off left-hander Patrick Sandoval (1-7). Jonny DeLuca smashed a two-run, bases-loaded double down the left-field line and Chandler Simpson followed with a two-run single. Sandoval began the inning by walking Yandy Diaz and Ryan Vilade, then surrendering a single to Junior Caminero.
CUBS 9, REDS 1
CINCINNATI (AP) — Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 45th home run as Chicago moved closer to clinching a postseason berth with a victory over Cincinnati.
Chicago (87-69) reduced its magic number to one and could wrap up a berth if the Diamondbacks lose to the Yankees later Sunday.
The Cubs began the day tied with the Padres and one game ahead of the Phillies for the top NL wild-card spot which would earn them home-field advantage in the wild-card round. The Cubs own the tiebreakers over the Diamondbacks, Padres, and Phillies.
Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman left Sunday’s game in the fourth inning after being struck in the face by a foul ball off the bat of Michael Busch while standing near the on-deck circle.
Cubs left-hander David Peterson (9-8) allowed a run on three hits in seven innings with one walk and seven strikeouts.
The Cubs loaded the bases with one out in the third. Ian Happ singled in a run and Nico Hoerner walked to force in another to extend Chicago’s lead to 3-0. Pedro Ramirez’s two-run single made the score 5-0.
Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder (6-12) allowed five earned runs on six hits with three walks and three strikeouts.
CARDINALS 5, NATIONALS 3
ST. LOUIS (AP) — Iván Herrera hit a pair of home runs, and Leo Bernal also homered as St. Louis scored three runs in the eighth inning to come from behind and beat Washington.
Bernal hit his fifth homer of the season off Yovanny Cruz (0-2) after Erik Tolman walked Jordan Walker with two outs in the eighth inning.
Herrera hit his second homer of the game and 18th of the season to tie the game at 3-all after hitting a solo shot in the first inning.
It was Herrera’s third career multi-homer game and second this season after going deep twice on June 13 at Minnesota.
Luis Gastelum (5-3) pitched a scoreless eighth inning for St. Louis, and Riley O’Brien pitched a perfect ninth to earn his National League-leading 38th save.
Cardinals starter Quinn Mathews allowed three runs on seven hits and two walks in a career-high seven innings.
Jake Irvin allowed two runs on three hits and had eight strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings for the Nationals.

The 2026 season could end up being Sonny Gray’s last.
The veteran right-hander, who turns 37 in November, has not committed to pitching in 2027 and recently told The Boston Globe he would retire “in a heartbeat” if his family wanted him to do so.
Boston reportedly is taking the possibility seriously, according to the outlet, with some in the organization believing retirement is on the table despite Gray’s strong season.
Asked recently about the possibility of retirement, Gray declined to say much.
“We can get into that at another time but not right now,” he said, per the Globe.
If 2026 is, indeed, his final big league season, Gray’s final start could come in the increasingly likely matchup against the rival Yankees during the wild-card round of the postseason.
Gray spent a season and a half in pinstripes after coming over before the 2017 trade deadline, and it didn’t go exactly as planned for either him or the team.
The three-time All-Star posted a 4.51 ERA across 41 games (34 starts) with the Yankees before being traded to Cincinnati before the 2019 season, during which he posted a Cy Young-caliber season with the Reds.
Gray ripped the Yankees during his introductory press conference with the Red Sox over the winter.
“It feels good to me to go to a place where it’s easy to hate the Yankees,” Gray said.
“I never wanted to go there in the first place.”
Gray is enjoying one of the best seasons of his 14-year MLB career in Beantown, posting a 2.82 ERA in 163 innings.
“I’ve very, very much so enjoyed Boston. Enjoyed the guys. Fenway has been, and is, a very special place,” Gray said.
